self_critique:
Run critique

What the harness/policy did suboptimally

- It converged too early after only three descendants and explored just two directions from the accepted parent. That is insufficient evidence that 0.603347 is near a local optimum.
- Node_002 achieved the highest reported point estimate (0.6036) but was rejected. If rejection was due to paired-seed uncertainty, the proper response was to gather more seeds or test nearby regularization strengths—not abandon the direction.
- Node_003 bundled too many changes: DeepFM, author-history features, context fields, dropout, and weight decay. A flat result is uninterpretable because beneficial and harmful components may have canceled.
- The hypotheses were overly specific about expected gains without enough supporting diagnostics. “Sparse-ID overfitting” was inferred mainly from an early validation peak; training curves, frequency-stratified performance, embedding norms, and per-user loss behavior were not reported.
- The search remained narrowly architecture/loss-focused. It did not test basic high-value controls such as regularization sweeps, embedding dimension, optimizer schedule, negative/slate weighting, or ensembling checkpoints/seeds.
- Reporting only rounded node scores obscures acceptance decisions. The journal should preserve per-seed paired deltas, confidence intervals, stopping epochs, and runtime. The baseline sigma of 0.0001 also deserves verification because it is unusually small relative to the observed gains.

What I would change in the scaffold

- Require each proposal to be atomic unless it is explicitly a staged package. Test DeepFM, history aggregation, context fields, dropout, and weight decay separately before combining them.
- Add an “uncertain but promising” branch state. A candidate with the best point estimate but insufficient significance should trigger replication rather than rejection.
- Use shared seeds and report paired deltas with confidence intervals. Allocate extra seeds adaptively when a result is close to the acceptance boundary.
- Log diagnostic artifacts: train/validation curves, best epochs, score by ID frequency bucket, embedding norms, calibration, and per-user logit means.
- Separate hypothesis generation from gain prediction; avoid unsupported numerical promises.
- Enforce broader exploration before convergence, for example several independent atomic branches plus at least one local hyperparameter sweep around the best accepted method.

What the next run should try first

Revisit node_002 first. Run a small sweep over frequency-adaptive regularization strength and functional form on top of node_001, using more paired seeds. Include ordinary uniform weight decay as a control and report results by user/item frequency bucket. The 0.6036 point estimate makes this the strongest unresolved lead.

If that does not replicate, test the node_003 components atomically, beginning with dropout/weight decay and then the causal history feature. DeepFM should come later because it adds complexity without evidence that the interaction order is currently limiting performance.
